rows.source: HSE wood-dust exposure and respiratory control
rows.verified: Wood dust can cause serious health problems and must be controlled as a substance hazardous to health.

rows.source: HSE wood-dust exposure and respiratory control
rows.verified: Hardwood dust can cause a rare form of nasal cancer.

rows.source: HSE wood-dust exposure and respiratory control
rows.verified: Wood dust is a recognised cause of occupational asthma.

rows.source: HSE wood-dust exposure and respiratory control
rows.verified: COSHH requires employers to prevent exposure to hazardous substances or, where prevention is not reasonably practicable, adequately control it.

rows.source: HSE wood-dust exposure and respiratory control
rows.verified: Local exhaust ventilation is a primary engineering control for capturing wood dust at source.

rows.source: HSE wood-dust exposure and respiratory control
rows.verified: Health surveillance is needed where workers remain at risk of occupational asthma from wood dust exposure.

rows.source: HSE wood-dust exposure and respiratory control
rows.verified: Cutting and sanding wood in construction can create high-risk dust exposure requiring effective controls.

rows.source: HSE wood-dust exposure and respiratory control
rows.verified: Respiratory protective equipment may be needed as a supplementary control where engineering controls do not fully control exposure.

rows.source: HSE wood-dust exposure and respiratory control
rows.verified: Wood-dust risk depends on wood species, process, dust concentration, particle size, exposure duration, extraction performance and worker susceptibility.

rows.source: HSE wood-dust exposure and respiratory control
rows.verified: HSE wood-dust evidence is process-, material-, workplace-, control-, worker- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.

rows.source: HSE nail-gun and powered-fastening safety
rows.verified: Nail guns include pneumatic tools and lighter electric or battery-powered designs with different operating characteristics.

rows.source: HSE nail-gun and powered-fastening safety
rows.verified: Safety devices fitted to nail guns can be defeated accidentally or intentionally, increasing injury risk.

rows.source: HSE nail-gun and powered-fastening safety
rows.verified: Users must understand how the tool should be used and how foreseeable failures and misuse can cause injury.

rows.source: HSE nail-gun and powered-fastening safety
rows.verified: Work equipment must be suitable for its intended use and safe for use under PUWER.

rows.source: HSE nail-gun and powered-fastening safety
rows.verified: Nail guns should be maintained in a safe condition and safety-critical features should be checked.

rows.source: HSE nail-gun and powered-fastening safety
rows.verified: Unexpected activation, ricochet, workpiece penetration and fastener deflection are foreseeable powered-fastening hazards.

rows.source: HSE nail-gun and powered-fastening safety
rows.verified: Operators should use the correct fasteners and operating settings specified for the tool and task.

rows.source: HSE nail-gun and powered-fastening safety
rows.verified: Cleaning, adjustment or maintenance should be carried out with the tool isolated from its energy source.

rows.source: HSE nail-gun and powered-fastening safety
rows.verified: Nail-gun risk depends on tool type, trigger system, pressure or power, fastener, workpiece, access, maintenance, training and user behaviour.

rows.source: HSE nail-gun and powered-fastening safety
rows.verified: HSE powered-fastening evidence is tool-, task-, fastener-, worker-, workplace- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
